chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: Tell me, regarding all that which was and all that which is to be until the Day of Judgment, was it not in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted? He said: Yes, before He created the heavens and the earth.

key_terms.التَّوْحِيدُ: Divine Unity / The Book of Unity

ai.seo_question: What does Shia Islam teach about God's knowledge of future events?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Ibn Abi Umair and Ibn Hazim, explicitly confirms that Allah's knowledge encompasses all temporal events—past, present, and future—prior to the act of creation. It serves as a cornerstone for the Shia doctrine of divine foreknowledge (al-Ilm al-Ilahi), distinguishing it from mere prescience by anchoring it in God's eternal essence before the emergence of time and space. This affirmation supports the theological balance between divine omniscience and human agency within the framework of al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/340] al-Tawhid: My father from Sa’d from Ibn Hashim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Hazim from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام.

He (Ibn Hazim) said: I said to him (the Imam): Consider all that which was and is to be up to the Day of Judgment - was it not in the knowledge of Allah the Elevated? He said: Yes. Before He created the Heavens and the Earth.
